title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
abstract: arXiv:2610.42001v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more capable and widely used, understanding when and how humans should work with these systems is becoming increasingly important. However, the empirical evidence in this space offers conflicting recommendations, which leaves individuals and organizations without clear guidance on when to combine human and AI capabilities. Existing meta-analyses can help reconcile these findings, but they require substantial manual effort and cannot readily incorporate new evidence as it emerges. To address this challenge, we introduce AutoAnalysis: an automated, self-updating meta-analysis of when humans and AI work better together, and when they work better alone. AutoAnalysis' most recent run synthesizes 1,955 effect sizes from 420 papers. translated_title: AutoAnalysis：一项关于人机协作的自动化、自我更新的元分析
translated_abstract: 随着生成式人工智能（AI）的能力不断提升和应用日益广泛，理解人类何时以及如何与这些系统协作正变得越来越重要。然而，该领域的实证研究得出了相互矛盾的建议，使得个人和组织无法就何时应结合人类与AI的能力获得明确的指导。现有的元分析可以帮助调和这些研究发现，但它们需要大量的人工工作，且无法随着新证据的出现而及时将其纳入。为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了AutoAnalysis：一项关于人类与AI何时协作更佳、何时单独工作更佳的自动化、自我更新的元分析。AutoAnalysis最近一次运行综合了来自420篇论文的1,955个效应量。在这批研究中，我们发现，平均而言，人机组合的表现显著优于人类单独工作，但其表现则显著更差（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出了AutoAnalysis——首个自动化、可自我更新的人机协作元分析系统，最新一次运行综合了420篇论文中的1,955个效应量，发现人机组合平均而言显著优于人类单独工作，从而解决了传统元分析依赖大量人工且无法及时纳入新证据的问题。
en_tdlr: AutoAnalysis is an automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration, whose latest run synthesizes 1,955 effect sizes from 420 papers and finds that human-AI combinations on average significantly outperform humans alone, addressing the heavy manual effort and inability to incorporate new evidence of traditional meta-analyses.
